title: Autoscaler leadership hotlock causing delayed reserved-pool replenishment and tenant starvation
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Production escalation: multiple customers reported sustained latency and token throttles during regional surge windows. Root behavior: the primary autoscaler leader enters a 'hotlock' state under specific lease-renewal jitter and metric-stitching conditions; this prevents timely reserved-pool replenishment and causes burst headroom starvation for small tenants. This ticket owns the bugfix, safety mitigations, canary rollout, and postmortem deliverables.
reproduction_steps: 1) Replay production traffic trace (trace-ID sample: trace-2026-02-06-XY) in staging against autoscaler-2.4.0 with a simulated AZ-affinity churn. 2) Inject metric-stitching delay (drop window between metrics collector and controller of 15-45s). 3) Create 3 tenants: large-tenant (high steady QPS), mid-tenant (sporadic bursts), small-tenant (microburst). 4) Observe leader renewals: leader will stop issuing preemptive headroom when lease-renewal jitter + stale metrics exceed threshold; reserved-pool allocator queue backs up and small-tenant requests are shed.
root_cause_summary: Race: leader election/renewal backoff path combined with metric staleness created a condition where the leader believes cluster headroom is sufficient (stale positive), while the allocator saw queued reservations and stopped replenishing due to a hotlock in the replenishment loop. Two contributing factors: (1) lease-ttl misalignment with metrics window; (2) allocator task queue not preemptible and lacked a watchdog to break long-running replenish cycles.
mitigations: Short-term (hotfix): 1) Force leader stepdown on controller if replenish loop exceeds 10s (temp guard). 2) Apply emergency config: reduce lease-ttl to 6s and align metrics window to 8s to avoid stale-positive. 3) Enable fallback routing for small-tenants to 'burst-capacity-fallback' pool for 72 hours. Long-term: 1) Rework replenish loop to be preemptible and add a watchdog + circuit-breaker. 2) Align lease and metrics windows and add strong invariants in leadership code. 3) Add unit + chaos tests to coverage.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge hotfix PR to autoscaler main with feature-gate 'hotlock_guard' disabled by default (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/1372). 2) Deploy to staging and run replay tests for 2h. 3) Canary in us-west-2 on 10% traffic for VIP customers for 6h. 4) If no regressions, increase to 50% for 24h then global. 5) Communication: notify ops Slack #dedicated-ops at each stage and send customer comms via CSMs for impacted tenants.
rollback_plan: Rollback uses standard release aliasing: if canary shows increased p99 latency or new errors > 0.5% in 15m windows, flip feature-gate off via runtime-config and roll autoscaler deployment back to previous replica set. Immediate mitigation: re-enable fallback routing and restore previous lease-ttl. Documented rollback steps are in the runbook (Confluence link).
monitoring_and_alerts: Add temporary alert: autoscaler.replenish_loop_duration > 10s for any leader (severity=P0). Dashboards: reserved_pool_headroom, tenant_request_shed_rate, leader_renewal_latency. Saved queries: PromQL sample: sum(rate(tenant_shed_total[5m])) by (tenant) > 0.01 for 5m. Post-deploy: observe these metrics for 48h.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Hotlock no longer reproducible in staging replay. 2) Canary rollout results show no p99 latency regression and reserved_pool_headroom does not drop below configured thresholds during simulated surge. 3) Small-tenant shed rate returns to baseline (<0.1% sustained). 4) New watchdog unit tests and a chaos test added to CI.
next_steps: Finish PR review and address security/code-review comments (assignee)
Coordinate canary window with SRE (ops-on-call: Mia Chen)
Update customer-facing KB with short-term workaround (owner: CSM team)
Schedule postmortem + retrospective within 3 business days of full rollout
